record.question: In GUI based Operating System design, the principle of ‘affordance’ means?
options: Interfaces should provide multiple ways to do the same action
The system provides feedback for every action
Interfaces should look consistent across apps
The design should suggest how an object can be used
record.explanation: D is the uniquely best answer in normal GUI design terminology: the design should make the available use/action perceptible. Don Norman explicitly says the design use of affordance was intended as perceived affordance and explains the relevance of what the user perceives in graphical interfaces. His later signifier terminology sharpens that distinction; it does not make A, B, or C correct definitions. Those options concern multiple methods, feedback, and consistency, respectively. Precision note: The GUI wording concerns perceived affordance; Norman's more precise later term for a cue communicating an action is signifier. Actual affordance and the visible cue are distinct concepts. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://jnd.org/affordances-and-design/; https://jnd.org/signifiers-not-affordances/

record.question: What does the “https://” part of a URL indicate?
options: The protocol used to transfer data
record.explanation: A is uniquely best. The https scheme identifies secure HTTP communication, whereas a URL's authority identifies the server and its path identifies the resource. RFC 9110 defines the https URI scheme for secured HTTP communication. Strictly, https is the scheme name and :// is syntax introducing the authority; saying that this URL part indicates the transfer protocol is a valid introductory interpretation. That syntax precision does not support the server-address, file-location, or search-engine distractors. Precision note: Strictly, https is the URI scheme, and :// introduces the authority. It indicates secure HTTP; this is distinct from the hostname and resource path. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-4.2.2

record.question: Which among the following is true about Primary vs Secondary memory?
options: Primary memory is non-volatile, Secondary memory is volatile
Primary memory is faster but temporary, Secondary memory is slower but permanent
Secondary memory directly communicates with CPU
record.explanation: B is the uniquely best printed comparison in the conventional primary-working-memory-versus-secondary-storage sense. NIELIT's original O-Level RAM lesson explicitly calls RAM primary/main/system memory, identifies its volatile retention and states it is faster than secondary memory. A reverses the volatility relationship, C falsely makes secondary storage volatile, and D is not the standard primary/secondary distinction. The terminology is broader in some classifications, which include nonvolatile ROM under primary storage, so the solution must explicitly state that this comparison concerns ordinary working RAM and must explain permanent as retention without power, not indefinite preservation. Precision note: Here primary means ordinary working RAM, and permanent means nonvolatile retention. Broader primary-storage taxonomies may also include nonvolatile ROM; secondary storage is not guaranteed to retain data forever. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://www.nielit.gov.in/gorakhpur/sites/default/files/Gorakhpur/OLevel_2_ICT_20mar.pdf; https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/primary-vs-secondary-storage

record.question: Which advanced MS Word feature allows automatic generation of citations and bibliography in different styles (APA, MLA, Chicago)?
record.explanation: B is uniquely best as a functional description of Word's reference/source-management feature. The stem asks which advanced feature performs a function; it does not quote an exact ribbon command or demand its literal UI label. Microsoft documents managing sources, inserting citations, choosing citation styles, and generating a bibliography. Track Changes, Insert Footnote, and Table of Authorities do not perform that bibliography-style workflow. The absence of a button literally named Reference Manager is a naming precision issue, not evidence that none of the printed choices describes the feature. Precision note: Reference Manager is a generic functional label here. In Word, use References → Manage Sources/Insert Citation/Bibliography (or the corresponding Citations pane), rather than searching for a universally named Reference Manager button. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/add-or-change-sources-citations-and-bibliographies; https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/project/academic/articles/new-feature-citation-list/

record.question: In networking, the primary function of a MAC address is
options: To uniquely identify a device on a local network
To locate websites on the Internet
To translate domain names into IP addresses
record.explanation: A is the uniquely best description of a MAC address's primary role: local link-layer addressing/identification for delivery. The other choices describe encryption, locating web resources, and DNS. Randomized or locally administered addresses do not change that role; they limit any claim that the address is an immutable globally unique identity. The phrase on a local network already supplies a local scope, and the option does not assert an eternal hardware serial number. Precision note: More precisely, a MAC address addresses a network interface on a link. It can be locally assigned or randomized and is not an immutable physical-device identity. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9724.html

record.question: Computer processing speed is usually expressed in?
record.explanation: C is the uniquely best printed answer for the ordinary processor-speed specification. Intel explicitly explains clock speed in GHz and distinguishes it from overall performance. The word usually and the supplied units support this normal introductory interpretation: bps and MB/s are data-transfer rates and DPI is spatial resolution. The imprecise umbrella phrase computer processing speed requires a visible explanation about clock frequency, but none of the alternatives is a comparably good processor clock unit. Precision note: GHz measures CPU clock frequency (billions of cycles per second), not overall performance by itself. Architecture, work per cycle, core count and workload also affect performance. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/gaming/resources/cpu-clock-speed.html
